target_customer: Consumers digitizing and sharing old family photos and building family trees
problem: Old printed photos and memories of relatives were scattered in shoeboxes and not shareable or organized.
business_model: Free consumer product with plans to monetize (paid scanning and storage); no revenue figures found
product_category: Consumer photo digitization and family history

founders.name: Rudy Adler
founders.background_notes: YC page lists later affiliation with Wealthsimple.

founders.name: Jonathan Good
founders.background_notes: YC page says he returned to New Zealand to work in ag, climate and health tech.

founders.name: Brett Huneycutt
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as co-founder of Wealthsimple (later).

exit.reason: Price not disclosed. All six employees joined Ancestry; the ShoeBox app had over 500,000 downloads and the service had about 260,000 users.

technical_complexity.rationale: Photo upload, sharing and a family tree feature, plus later an iPhone scanning app, were standard consumer engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Stored family photos create some lock-in, but nothing prevented Ancestry or Facebook from adding the same features.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Ancestry.com acquired the company in October 2012 and folded its photo features into Ancestry; the site was reportedly shut in late 2013.

market_need_then: Genealogy was a large paid category led by Ancestry, and family photos were not well served by public social networks. The company later had about 260,000 users at acquisition.

branding.domain_note: Used 1000memories.com (numeral form); the domain now redirects to a parked page.

identity.voice_and_tone: Warm and memorial, aimed at remembering people who have died

branding.brand_signature: Shoebox, the later app name, reused by Ancestry

brand_strength.rationale: Tech press covered the funding and the Facebook for the past angle; the memorial theme was emotional but the brand was folded into Ancestry within two years.

pivots.from: Digital memorial sites for deceased relatives
pivots.to: A feed and iPhone app for old family photos, described as a Facebook for the past
pivots.why: Per TechCrunch, the company expanded beyond memorials; the founders' reasoning was not captured.

outcome_analysis: 1000memories raised 2.5 million dollars from Greylock and well known angels in February 2011, pivoted from memorial pages to a photo feed and scanning app, and was acquired by Ancestry.com in October 2012 with about 260,000 users. The product was reportedly shut down in late 2013 with features absorbed into Ancestry, so the exit looks like a strategic feature buy rather than a standalone success.
notes: The 2.5M round is called Series A only by an aggregator, so it is recorded as other. Unverified: aggregator lists a 15K seed in 2010 and total funding of 3M (one Xconomy article) versus about 2.5M. Lead investor is listed as Greylock by TechCrunch but Ron Conway by one aggregator. The dataset website field points to ancestry.com. No dated competitor sources found for 2010, so competitors are empty. Education and prior employers for founders were not found on pages I opened (Wikipedia mentions Rhodes scholarships and McKinsey and Wieden+Kennedy but I did not open the article). Shutdown date of late 2013 comes from Wikipedia and a mirror.
